text:
This supermarket has the decent choice of fruits and vegetables. It is spacious and quite conveniently located. It is also cheap.

So why one star then? Well, there are two reasons for it.

1) They sell nearly spoiled or spoiled food. Sometimes, with a discount. Sometimes, without mentioning that it has almost expired. I bought around 1 kg of chicken, just to open it at home and throw away since it was smelly already. Food poisoning? No thanks!

2) The staff never say hello, thank you or any other simple courtesy. Not included into their basic rules, I guess. Also it is quite difficult to find someone for assistance.

Therefore, ❌
Highly recommended.

I'm thinking that Lotus has improved their stocking over the past couple of years since I first reviewed it. They get a 4th star. I haven't had a problem with finding things on my more recent shopping expeditions there. The entire centre is worth a visit, it's not far from the many attractions and giant shopping malls of Siam but offers a look at a more typical modern Thai shopping centre with a good range of stores alongside the Lotus hypermarket, as well as food outlets including an excellent food court.

For the record, here's my original review from 2 years ago, written ~mid 2024:

Poor stocking of shelves. Items run out. I'd buy more if it was there.

To the slightly chubby female employee in the blue shirt who answered my question, and to inform the supervisor of the electronics sales department in the evenings: A customer wanted to buy a fan, but the employee said they couldn't test it because they had already tested all the models. The customer then asked, "What if it's broken when I get home? Who will be responsible for the return and exchange?" The employee simply replied, "Based on my salary," and I'm not sure how they've been trained. They just said, "If it's broken, you can exchange it within xxx days." The point is, why should the customer have to return it? They should be allowed to test it on the spot.

Please provide better training. Or perhaps they lack customer service skills because they don't sell this particular product.

This is in stark contrast to the male employees at Home Pro Samyan Mitrtown, who are incredibly dedicated to selling and answering questions.
